lead.event: SGX RegCo's prospectus review and listing-rule changes
lead.headline: SGX RegCo takes over prospectus reviews from 4 January 2027
lead.blurb: MAS will delegate reviews of Mainboard and Global Listing Board prospectuses to SGX RegCo, which will also abolish the Listing Advisory Committee. Companies can file listing applications and prospectuses through one electronic platform instead of filing separately with both regulators. SGX RegCo aims to keep reviews to six to eight weeks with greater certainty, while MAS will continue approving disclosure waivers and overseeing SGX RegCo’s regulatory performance. The changes follow recommendations from the securities market review group.

deals_control.event: Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio's proposed buyout of Delfin family stakes
deals_control.headline: Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio proposes €3.7 billion each to buy out Delfin heirs
deals_control.blurb: The plan covers the seven other shareholders, with a reported €22 billion loan from Citigroup backing it. It is due to be presented on 7 November and aims to block Michal Strnad's offer for at least 62.5% of Delfin at a 30% discount to net asset value.

deals_control.event: Daiwa House Logistics Trust's Sendai divestment and Hiroshima acquisition
deals_control.headline: Daiwa House Logistics Trust plans JPY13.5 billion Sendai sale and Hiroshima buy
deals_control.blurb: It will sell DPL Sendai Port to sponsor Daiwa House Industry for JPY13.5 billion and acquire DPL Hiroshima Itsukaichi Port from a third party for JPY8.2 billion. The property is fully leased to two logistics firms and has a 5.7% implied NPI yield, with unitholder approval required at an EGM soon.

deals_control.event: Sunray Singapore's sale of QT Singapore hotel
deals_control.headline: Sunray Singapore sells QT Singapore hotel for over S$260 million
deals_control.blurb: The undisclosed family office paid more than S$1.94 million per key. Since reopening in September 2024, the hotel has achieved occupancy of around 90% and average daily room rates exceeding S$400.

deals_control.event: IOI Properties' planned Singapore real estate fund
deals_control.headline: IOI Properties plans Singapore real estate fund, 50% stake could raise nearly RM10 billion
deals_control.blurb: Chief executive Datuk Lee Yeow Seng said the fund will be backed by the developer’s Singapore assets. IOI Properties has begun marketing it to investors and plans to launch it within the next few months.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: STT GDC's talks for a S$3.1 billion syndicated loan
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: STT GDC talks with banks for S$3.1 billion syndicated loan
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The three-year facility would finance its assets, with a 165 basis point margin over the Singapore Overnight Rate Average and an option to extend by up to two years. Standard Chartered, UOB, OCBC and DBS are global coordinators, mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners.

capital_raising_buybacks.headline: Mapletree Investments' planned Singapore IPO could raise at least S$1 billion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: People familiar with the matter say Mapletree Investments has picked Citigroup, DBS and Morgan Stanley to work on the IPO, but has not decided which assets to include. A listing could take place as soon as next year, though its timing and size may change and more banks may be added.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: mm2 Asia creditors' approval of its debt repayment scheme
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: mm2 Asia secures creditor approval for debt repayment scheme with 75% backing
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The scheme includes a share placement to raise about S$15 million and new shares for some creditors as partial debt settlement. It still requires shareholder approval and court sanction, and mm2 Asia’s moratorium has been extended to 21 November.

earnings_guidance.event: UOB's Q3 FY2026 results miss forecasts and prompt analyst reactions
earnings_guidance.headline: UOB posts S$1.25 billion Q3 profit below forecasts as five brokers cut targets
earnings_guidance.blurb: Profit rose 182.2% year on year but fell short of the S$1.38 billion consensus of six Bloomberg-polled analysts. The target cuts followed UOB’s guidance that full-year net interest margin would be below its earlier 1.75% to 1.8% range.

earnings_guidance.event: DBS's Q3 FY2026 results, dividend and analyst reactions
earnings_guidance.headline: DBS reports Q3 net profit of S$2.81 billion, down 5% year on year
earnings_guidance.blurb: It declared a dividend of S$0.81 per share, including a S$0.15 capital return dividend, compared with S$0.75 a year earlier. Six brokerages cut their target prices to between S$76.40 and S$88, while DBS expects mid-single-digit total income growth in 2027.

earnings_guidance.event: Great Eastern's Q3 FY2026 net profit decline
earnings_guidance.headline: Great Eastern's Q3 net profit falls 72% to S$102.9 million
earnings_guidance.blurb: The decline was mainly due to negative financial-market movements and a S$57.1 million loss from the completed partial sale of Great Eastern Life Indonesia to OCBC Indonesia, substantially offset by a S$52.6 million reclassification gain. Great Eastern expects investment conditions to remain challenging in the near to medium term.

earnings_guidance.headline: CapitaLand Investment reports 3% fall in nine-month revenue to S$1.5 billion
earnings_guidance.blurb: Property investment revenue fell 23% to S$580 million, while fee-related revenue rose 15% to S$1.04 billion. The decline followed divestments and deconsolidation, including the end of contributions from Synergy and Dalian IT Park, partly offset by One iPark.

other.event: Yangzijiang Maritime Development's orders for 11 new vessels
other.headline: Yangzijiang Maritime orders 11 new vessels
other.blurb: The orders are with several Chinese shipyards and comprise seven LR2 product tankers and four bulk carriers, with delivery expected between 2029 and 2030. Including these, Yangzijiang Maritime has signed contracts for 18 new vessels worth US$808 million over 10 months, and its orderbook will grow to 111 vessels, including 86 confirmed orders under construction.

other.event: CSE Global's Q3 FY2026 new orders rose to S$434.9 million
other.headline: CSE Global's Q3 FY2026 new orders rise to S$434.9 million
other.blurb: Electrification orders rose 937% year on year to S$320.3 million, including two US contracts worth S$254.8 million. The order book stood at S$728.5 million at 30 September, up 55.8% from a year earlier.

other.event: EC World REIT's failed retrial application over its asset pledge ruling
other.headline: EC World REIT fails to win asset pledge retrial, with RMB222.5 million contingent liability
other.blurb: The ruling concerned the unauthorised pledge of its Fuzhou E-Commerce asset to Hangzhou Fuyang financial institutions. The contingent liability is unchanged from the revised figure announced on 25 September, though it may still be adjusted. The trust's earlier appeal was rejected by the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court in February.
